subject: Biology
title: Sex Determination Across Species
description: A 60-second lesson on Sex Determination Across Species.

hook.text: In humans, chromosomes decide sex. In crocodiles, temperature does. Evolution invented many methods.

buildup.text: Mammals use XX/XY chromosomes. Birds use ZW/ZZ. Many reptiles use nest temperature.

discovery.text: Clownfish are all born male. When the dominant female dies, the largest male becomes female.

twist.text: Some whiptail lizard species are all female—reproducing by parthenogenesis without any males at all.

climax.text: Sex determination systems evolve rapidly. Even closely related species can use different mechanisms.

punchline.text: Male, female, or neither. Nature decides many ways.

quiz.question: What determines sex in many reptiles?

details.summary: Sex determination varies remarkably across species. Mammals use XY chromosomes, birds use ZW systems, and many reptiles determine sex by egg incubation temperature. Some fish change sex during their lifetime, and certain lizard species are entirely female, reproducing by parthenogenesis.
details.whyItMatters: Diverse sex determination mechanisms reveal that what seems biologically fundamental is actually evolutionarily flexible. Climate change threatens species with temperature-dependent sex determination by skewing offspring sex ratios.
takeaways: Mammalian sex is determined by the SRY gene on the Y chromosome
Many reptile species use incubation temperature to determine offspring sex
Some fish species routinely change sex in response to social conditions

faq.question: How could climate change affect species with temperature-dependent sex?
faq.answer: Rising temperatures could skew sex ratios dramatically. Sea turtle nests in warming sand produce nearly all females. If warming continues, some populations may lack males entirely, threatening reproduction and potentially driving extinction of affected species.

faq.question: How do fish change sex?
faq.answer: In sequential hermaphroditism, individuals change sex based on social cues. Clownfish are born male; the largest female's death triggers the dominant male to become female. Wrasses reverse this. Hormonal and gene expression changes drive the physical transformation.
